review.brief_reason: The first change (5*x2/x5 + 4*x4/x5 -> (5*x2+4*x4)/x5) is algebraically equivalent under real semantics. The second change (sin(5*x2/x5 + 5*x4/x5) -> sin(5*(x2+x4)/x5)) is also equivalent. The third change (sin(5*x2/x5 + 4*x4/x5) -> sin((5*x2+4*x4)/x5)) is equivalent. The fourth change (sin(x1/x5 + 6*x2/x5 + 6*x4/x5 + (x2/x5 + x4 + (x2+4/x5)/x1)/x5) -> sin((x1+6*x2+7*x4+x2/x5+(x2+x4/x5)/x1)/x5)) is NOT equivalent: the original has 6*x4/x5 plus x4/x5 (from the nested term x4/x5), totaling 7*x4/x5, which matches. But the original also has x2/x5 (from the nested term) plus 6*x2/x5 = 7*x2/x5, while the proposed has 6*x2/x5 + x2/x5 = 7*x2/x5. Wait, rechecking: original = x1/x5 + 6*x2/x5 + 6*x4/x5 + (x2/x5 + x4 + (x2+x4/x5)/x1)/x5 = x1/x5 + 6*x2/x5 + 6*x4/x5 + x2/x5^2 + x4/x5 + (x2+x4/x5)/(x1*x5). Proposed = (x1+6*x2+7*x4+x2/x5+(x2+x4/x5)/x1)/x5 = x1/x5 + 6*x2/x5 + 7*x4/x5 + x2/x5^2 + (x2+x4/x5)/(x1*x5). Original has 6*x4/x5 + x4/x5 = 7*x4/x5. These match. All transformations are algebraically valid.
